thread:
alexa-cs: FYI we have a customer escalation — upgraded to python-sdk 2.4.0 yesterday and saw a huge jump in billed tokens and latency spikes. They say multiple identical completions were generated. Attached log & minimal repro. Can eng help triage?

maya-support: Thanks — can you paste the customer account id and a sample request/response (sanitized) so we can repro?

alexa-cs: account: acct_ABC123 (prod). Customer ran this snippet after pip upgrade:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key="...")
rc.generate("Summarize this long doc...", model="rwd-1-large")
```
They see 2 responses and double token usage for a single call. Logs: `req=01E9F2X9 id=rid_7a9 redirect=307 -> /shard-17` then `req=01E9F2X9 id=rid_7a9 sent_again status=200`

sam-sdk: pinging in. Do we have the SDK release notes handy? I recall a change around how we handle redirects in 2.4.0 (follow_redirects default flipped). If follow_redirects was made true and we don't carry idempotency across a 307 redirect, a POST could get replayed against a shard without the idempotency header — explains duplicate completions and billing.

liam-eng: 307s are for shard routing (we redirect to storage/proxy). Historically we rewrote to a signed GET for large artifacts, but for streaming/generate endpoints we want to preserve headers. If the client follows redirect automatically and removes x-redwood-idempotency, server will accept repeat.

maya-support: customer pinned back to 2.3.2 and reports no more duplicates. Can we confirm workaround and next steps?

sam-sdk: quick repro I've run locally: `curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' -H 'Idempotency-Key: test-1'` returns `307 Location: https://shard-host/...` then some clients auto-POST to the Location without Idempotency-Key. Python's http lib in our wrapper changed behavior in 2.4.0: we enabled Session.follow_redirects by default to reduce 302 hops, but we didn't preserve idempotency header across redirects.

sam-sdk: Workarounds: 1) pin to `redwood==2.3.2` (confirmed working), or 2) set env `REDWOOD_PY_FOLLOW_REDIRECTS=false` (temporary flag we still honor) so client will return redirect to caller instead of auto-follow.

ops-oncall: Can we find impacted customers by searching logs for requests with the same request id followed by immediate repeated accepted responses? Query idea: `select * from ingress where request_id like 'rid_%' and attempts > 1 and header:idempotency is NULL` — ops can run.

liam-eng: We'll also add server-side guard: treat redirects as requiring idempotency check and return 409 if missing; but that's a little risky for existing clients. Prefer fix in SDK to preserve headers across 307s.

sam-sdk: PR created: GH #6543 — ensure idempotency header is preserved across redirects and restore previous follow_redirects default until we have full telemetry. I'll get a patch for 2.4.1.

deploy-bot: Canary build of python-sdk 2.4.1 scheduled for 1712009000 (UTC). Will notify when canary completes.

maya-support: Customer pinned and billing spike stopped. They want ETA on patched release so they can upgrade from pinned version.

sam-sdk: ETA: hotfix release 2.4.1 within ~4 hours if canary is green. We'll also ship a short KB explaining root cause + recommended pin/flag.

ops-oncall: Running the query now across last 48h to enumerate impacted accounts; will post results in this thread in ~30m.

alexa-cs: Thanks team. Please add the KB to the support playbook and let CS know when 2.4.1 is out. Customer would like invoice credit for the excess tokens — please advise billing.

maya-support: Looping in billing separately. @billing-team can you review acct_ABC123 token spike and advise? (reacted with :eyes:)

sam-sdk: Quick note for repro: minimal curl that reproduces on my machine included `-L` (follow redirects). Without `-L` (no auto-follow) I only see single invocation. So the pattern is consistent.

liam-eng: Also adding a one-line trace in our ingress proxies to copy Idempotency-Key into the Location redirect meta so clients that follow will still see it (defense in depth).

ops-oncall: Impacted accounts query done: 7 accounts flagged with >2x token delta and repeated request patterns. Posting list to Ops ticket OPP-992 (internal).

alexa-cs: resolving for now — customer pinned and is happy with rollback/temporary fix. Keeping thread open until canary and release validated. :thumbsup:
